Q: Why is my application not working, and why isn't the private node screen in VS Code displaying as expected? A: If you encounter issues with the application not working, follow these steps: Open Command Prompt and type ipconfig to check your current IP address. Compare the IP address displayed with the one maintained in the hosts file. If the IP address in the hosts file does not match the current IP, update the hosts file with the correct IP address. After saving the changes, restart the application and check if the issue is resolved. This will help ensure that the correct IP address is mapped for proper application functionality.

documents.t: FAQs on Private Node Date of Issue: March 2025 Target Audience: Application Developers Prepared by: RINCY MERIN ROBINSON Platform Version: 7.0

Q: I'm getting a "JavaScript heap out of memory" / "FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit" error when running tsc -w in Private Node. What's causing this and how do I fix it? A: This typically happens when your system doesn't have enough free RAM left for the TypeScript watcher to allocate memory — often because browsers (Chrome/Edge) or other applications are already consuming most of the available memory. On an 8GB machine, it's common to see 7GB+ already in use before the compiler even starts. Immediate fix: Close unused browser tabs/windows and other memory-heavy applications before starting a tsc -w session. Alternatively, give Node a defined heap budget so it fails more gracefully or succeeds where the default limit was too aggressive: set NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 tsc -w If the issue persists or recurs frequently: A RAM upgrade (16GB recommended) is advised for machines regularly running Private Node builds alongside browsers/IDEs. Check that tsconfig.json includes incremental: true and skipLibCheck: true to reduce the compiler's memory footprint per rebuild. Use cmd terminal to start the typescript watcher (tsc -w).

documents.t: Q: Why is it important for the port number in the private node server to match the port number in the private URL when opening the application in the browser? A: It is crucial for the port number in the private node server to match the port number in the private URL because: The port number in the URL defines which specific service or application on the server is being accessed. If the port numbers don't match, the browser will attempt to connect to the wrong service, potentially resulting in an error or failure to load the application correctly. Ensuring that both the server configuration and the private URL use the same port number guarantees proper communication and accessibility between the client (browser) and the server. Mismatched port numbers can lead to incorrect routing or connection failures, preventing the application from loading as expected after selecting the "Open Application in Browser" option. Note: Always verify that the port number shown in the URL matches the one configured on the server to avoid connectivity issues.

documents.t: Q: Private node setup failing, getting the below error. A: The above error is shown when node_modules are not maintained Globally or missing some required files. You can continue with any of the below steps For installing node_modules locally for a private node (Windows/ Mac): open command palette(Ctrl + Shift + P) and run “Set Local Package Installation” to enabled. Notification for enabled/disabled will be shown in the bottom right corner. It can also be seen in the vs code settings(search for Local Package Installation). For Installing node_modules globally and maintain the paths in Windows : open command palette(Ctrl + Shift + P) and run “Run Environment Setup”, select all and press OK, it will ask for admin password. This will do the host file entry if not present, maintain environment variables for your user, do node_module installation globally, and also install the certificate needed. “Run Environment Setup”

documents.t: Q: Unable to start the server in the javascript debug terminal A: By default the javascript debug terminal commands will be executed in the powershell. As of node version 22.X.X, direct execution of the npm command is restricted. To start the server in the JavaScript Debug Terminal, follow the steps outlined below, open the javascript debug terminal Execute the ‘cmd’ command Start the server with ‘npm run kloServerStart’ command

This is a screen that helps the users search for the frequently asked questions and read the details. It can also be used as a guide on the process of performing certain activities in the application.
App to be assigned: faqs_1 faqs_1 app should be assigned to the user.

Go to the Help Center menu and click on the sub-menu named Help Center to open it. The screen will be initially loaded with the FAQ groups based on their sequence in ascending order. Users can search for the FAQs based on their group title, question, key ID and key description. Users need to input the search text and click on the OK button to perform the search. Users can clear the search criteria by clicking on the cross Button in the Search Bar. Users can Expand Any Group To See the List of Questions Associated with that Group. Users Can Click On the Question Link To Open The Answer Detail Section. Users Can Also See the Answer in Full-Screen Mode by Clicking on the Expand Button at the Bottom Right Hand Side of the Answer Section. Users can close the full-screen answer by clicking on the collapse button at the bottom right-hand side. Users can close the answer detail by clicking on the close button on the top right-hand side of the answer detail.
This can be used to: Search for the user-relevant FAQs and to read their answers in detail.
